review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Dwellings, residential buildings, apartments, building components and rooms with combined uses; correct genus/part-whole confusion and unsupported universal features.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Cambridge Dictionary entries independently check housing senses and regional distinctions. Full definitions are not copied; qualified labels and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: New concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Dwelling is a physical place serving residential use; a house here is a whole residential building and an apartment a unit within a building. Legal eligibility, ownership, tenure and occupancy rules are outside scope.

sense_decisions.scope: A physical place designed or used for people to reside in. Do not restrict it to a whole building, legal housing unit, current occupancy or a structure fixed to land.
A residential building divided into apartment units. The building contains apartments; it is not itself one apartment.
A whole residential building with two apartment units. Distinguish this meaning of duplex from a two-level apartment and from one semi-detached dwelling.
A residential house standing separately from adjacent houses. Detached does not by itself imply one family or one apartment.
One residential house in a connected row. Do not identify a row house with the entire terrace or a house having an outdoor terrace.
Use the British sense of one house adjoining one other house. Do not copy the dictionary duplex synonym as identity with a whole two-unit building.
A residential house with one storey in the selected ordinary sense. Do not import bungalow or cottage as exact synonyms.
Restrict the house family to buildings with a basement rather than asserting one for every house.
Restrict the house family to buildings with an attic rather than asserting one for every house.
A dwelling that includes a balcony; a functional/component classification independent of whole-building versus apartment unit.
A building with a balcony, without treating balcony presence as universal for buildings.
A whole residential building with a balcony.
An apartment that includes a balcony. This does not make the whole building an apartment.
One apartment occupying two levels. Distinguish its layout from a whole building divided into two apartments; do not require a particular access mechanism.
An apartment whose principal living functions share a main room, with separate sanitary facilities. Do not equate one bedroom with one total room.
An apartment with one bedroom. This does not state the total room count or translate the Russian one-room-apartment category.
A boat designed or used as a dwelling. Broaden the dictionary barge-only wording; do not classify every floating dwelling as a navigable boat or this boat as a land building.
A room used for living in, distinct from every room in general and from an entire apartment.
A room intended for dining, distinct from a public canteen or food-service organization.
One room serving both kitchen and dining-room functions.
One room serving sleeping and sitting/living functions. Select the room use, not necessarily a separate rented apartment or a self-contained bedsit.
One room serving bathing and toilet functions. Do not require both a bathtub and a shower.
A bedroom intended to accommodate guests; distinguish it from every guest reception room.
A room intended for washing laundry, not the commercial laundry business or a compulsory feature of every dwelling.

The enclosed vertical building space containing a staircase, distinct from the steps themselves, the central open void, an elevator shaft or a single landing. No fire-safety classification or enclosure standard is imported.
A platform within or at the end of a flight of stairs. Exclude aircraft landing, boat landing and the full staircase.
A building with stairs. Not every building requires stairs.
A whole residential building with stairs, without assuming that every house has them.
Existing postroika/building may be a broader built structure; do not merge it solely from its English spelling.
Reuse the existing childrens-room record later rather than importing nursery as a new synonym without age scope.
Step is ambiguous between architectural step and abstract stage; do not merge it with step 1895 in this cohort.
Portable and fixed ladders need a distinct instrument review; do not import them as exact staircase synonyms.
The dictionary equates cottage and bungalow in a single-storey gloss, but wider usage differs. Add only the explicit single-storey house family now.
Duplex apartment and whole two-unit building remain distinct records and are not given an unqualified duplex alias.

review.limits: No universal basement, attic, balcony, staircase, corridor, separate bedroom or separate living room on every house/building. Do not identify bedroom count with Russian total-room count, bungalow with all cottages, or the two meanings of duplex. Existing garage/structure, premises/space, house/school, tree/wood and other component/material percentages remain queued. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Retain the selected whole-house/apartment-unit exclusion and repair the wrong apartment genus. Reject bedroom/living-room and bathroom/toilet exclusions before adding their reviewed combined-use subtypes.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing residential premises, residing, building components, stairs, storey, apartments and established rooms are reused.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
